**European Parliament votes to advance digital euro to final negotiations**

*The full Parliament's backing moves the digital euro into trilogue, setting up the decisive phase of negotiations that will determine whether a CBDC launches by 2029.*

The European Parliament voted in favour of creating a digital euro, following the ECON committee's earlier endorsement of its negotiating mandate in June. The vote authorises the Parliament's team to enter trilogue discussions with the Council of the EU and the European Commission.

The timeline now points toward a potential 2029 launch, though substantive disagreements remain on issues such as holding limits, the role of intermediaries and the relationship between the digital euro and private payment schemes. The trade body representing open banking providers warned in June that the current legislative text could exclude them from distribution, a concern that trilogue negotiations will need to address.

For banks and payment service providers, the vote converts the digital euro from a policy discussion into a concrete legislative track. Firms that have not yet begun assessing their distribution, liquidity and technical readiness now face a narrowing window before the regulatory framework is finalised.

*Sources: [European Parliament backs digital euro, paving way for final negotiations](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48068/european-parliament-backs-digital-euro-paving-way-for-final-negotiations) — Finextra*

**Citi expands cross-border instant payments network to 300 partner banks**

*Citigroup is opening its cross-border instant payments infrastructure to correspondent banking partners, a move that extends real-time settlement reach well beyond its own direct client base.*

Citigroup announced it is expanding its international instant payments network to partner banks, with around 300 institutions now integrated into the service. The network serves multinational corporate clients through Citi's Services division, allowing them to initiate and receive cross-border payments that settle in real time.

The expansion reflects a broader shift in which large correspondent banks are positioning instant payment connectivity as a competitive differentiator in transaction banking. Rather than building proprietary networks from scratch, partner banks gain access to Citi's existing real-time rails across multiple corridors.

For European banks and corporates, the move adds another cross-border instant payments option alongside initiatives such as the ECB's cross-currency TIPS pilot and Swift's own real-time ambitions. It also underscores the growing expectation among corporate treasurers that cross-border payments should match the speed domestic instant payments already offer.

*Sources: [Citigroup expands cross-border instant payments to partner banks](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/citigroup-expands-cross-border-instant-payments-partner-banks-2026-07-09/) — Reuters*

**Seventeen banks prepare live transactions on Swift's shared ledger**

*Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger moves from sandbox to live pilot, with 17 banks across six countries testing tokenised deposits for round-the-clock payment availability.*

Seventeen banks from six countries will begin piloting live transactions on Swift's interoperable shared ledger, using tokenised deposits to enable 24/7 payment availability and improve liquidity efficiency. The pilot marks a transition from the experimental phase Swift has been running since late 2025 into a production environment with real value at stake.

The shared ledger is designed to sit alongside existing correspondent banking infrastructure rather than replace it, allowing banks to move tokenised commercial bank money across the Swift network without requiring counterparties to adopt the same distributed ledger technology. That interoperability-first approach distinguishes it from standalone tokenisation platforms that require bilateral integration.

The pilot's progress will be closely watched as a signal of whether tokenised deposits can deliver practical benefits in wholesale payments, or whether the technology remains better suited to securities settlement. For European banks already navigating the ECB's digital euro preparations and the BIS's Project Aperta work, Swift's shared ledger represents another infrastructure layer they may need to engage with in the near term.

*Sources: [Banks to pilot live transactions on Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48060/banks-to-pilot-live-transactions-on-swifts-blockchain-based-shared-ledger) — Finextra*

**French Banking Federation frames payment sovereignty as strategic priority**

*France's banking lobby has publicly positioned European payment autonomy as a strategic imperative, adding political weight to the sovereignty argument driving EPI and the digital euro.*

The French Banking Federation has set out its view that payment sovereignty should be treated as a strategic priority for Europe, echoing and reinforcing similar arguments made earlier this year by the Bank of Finland and the ECB's Piero Cipollone. The intervention adds the weight of France's commercial banking sector to a debate that has largely been framed by central banks and policymakers.

The Federation's stance comes as several parallel initiatives compete to reduce European dependence on non-European card schemes and payment infrastructure. EPI's Wero is expanding into its fifth market, the digital euro is advancing through the Parliament, and Visa has responded with a €500 million European investment pledge. France's banks, several of which are EPI shareholders, have a direct commercial interest in the outcome.

The framing is notable for its explicitness. Where banks have previously supported sovereignty initiatives through participation, the Federation is now articulating payment independence as a matter of strategic necessity, aligning the private sector's public messaging with the political narrative that European institutions have been building throughout 2026.

*Sources: [French Banking Federation frames payment sovereignty as strategic priority](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48068/european-parliament-backs-digital-euro-paving-way-for-final-negotiations) — Finextra*
